design_gotchas.title: Push-Pull Output Cannot Be Wired-AND or Pulled Up to a Higher Logic Rail
design_gotchas.detail: TLV7011 actively drives OUT to VCC and VEE (VOH 4.8 V typ at 3 mA, 5 V). Output abs max is VCC + 0.3 V, so tying a pull-up to a higher rail or paralleling outputs as a wired-AND fights the high-side FET. Use the open-drain TLV7021 (same DBV pinout) for level translation or bus sharing.

design_gotchas.title: Only 5.5 V Recommended Supply Max (6 V Abs Max) vs 30 V LM393-Class Comparators
design_gotchas.detail: The single-channel TLV7011 is limited to 1.6 V-5.5 V recommended and 6 V absolute maximum. Dropping it onto a 12 V or 24 V LM393DR/LMV331 board socket destroys the part; it only suits 1.8 V-5 V logic rails (the dual TLV7012/22 has a separate 6.5 V/7 V rating).

design_gotchas.title: Internal Hysteresis of 4.2 mV Typ Is Always On — Do Not Double-Count With External Feedback
design_gotchas.detail: VHYS = 4.2 mV typ (1.2 mV min, 14 mV max) is built in. Slow inputs get a clean edge without external feedback, but the trip-point shift of up to ±7 mV plus 8 mV max offset must be budgeted in precision thresholds; add external positive feedback only for hysteresis larger than ~14 mV.

design_gotchas.title: Input Clamp to VEE: Current-Limit Any Input Swinging 0.3 V Below Ground
design_gotchas.detail: Inputs are diode-clamped to VEE, and inputs able to swing 0.3 V below VEE must be limited to 10 mA or less. Series resistors are mandatory when sensing bipolar or connector-exposed signals. Input range extends to VCC + 0.1 V at VS ≥ 2.5 V, so no phase reversal occurs in-range.

design_gotchas.title: SOT-23-5 RθJA = 306.3 °C/W and 1.6 V / 20 µs Power-Up Window
design_gotchas.detail: Package is thermally weak but dissipation is tiny at 5 µA Iq. The output is only valid after VS exceeds 1.6 V for tON = 20 µs; during slow supply ramps the output state is indeterminate, so gate downstream logic with a reset or delay.

typical_use_cases: Micropower undervoltage/overvoltage threshold detectors on 1.8 V-5 V battery rails
IR receiver analog front ends and zero-crossing detectors with clean 5 ns edges
Window comparators and level discriminators with internal 4.2 mV hysteresis
Portable and wearable fault monitors needing 5 µA supply current and 260 ns response
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TLV7011DBVR is a single push-pull, rail-to-rail-input comparator in a 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV) package for 1.6 V-5.5 V supplies, rated -40°C to 125°C. It combines 5 µA supply current, 260 ns/310 ns propagation delay, 4.2 mV internal hysteresis and no phase reversal on overdriven inputs. Its pinout (1 OUT, 2 VEE, 3 IN+, 4 IN-, 5 VCC) matches TLV3201, but it is not a supply-compatible replacement for open-collector 30 V LM393/LMV331 parts.
